ai_technology: Agentic Inventory-Policy Discovery System; LLM-guided symbolic search

evidence.ai_role: LLMs propose structured symbolic policy edits using evaluation feedback; numerical parameter fitting and cost evaluation are separate.
evidence.tested: Numerical evaluation across four inventory settings and an analytical cost-gap proof for a restricted three-period lost-sales case.
evidence.unknown: No real-world deployment, general optimality or separate-team/proof-kernel confirmation established in reviewed material. Prior related LLM-guided inventory work is acknowledged.

organization: New York University; Tsinghua University; Beijing Institute of Mathematical Sciences and Applications

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 metadata; HTML Introduction/related work, Theorem6.3 and proof9.3, policy-search implementation and evaluation constraints.

summary: A preprint reports LLM-guided symbolic inventory-policy discovery and numerical evaluation across 15,600 instances. The authors prove a capped dual-shortfall specialization has lower long-run cost than the specified adjacent-integer capped-base-stock benchmark family in a three-period lost-sales setting under restrictive small-mean integer-demand and cost-ratio assumptions. LLMs propose formula edits; a numerical engine fits and tests candidates. The analytical proof is source-reported, without proof-kernel checking or independent confirmation established here; the result does not establish global optimality, real-world savings or first priority for LLM policy discovery.
title: LLM-discovered inventory rule improves a bounded cost benchmark
